items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: But it started by Henry Martin and Black Bennett. They didn't want to start that. They just told us to light out on the blues and we did it.

ctx.x: Yeah, them kind of people, they were playing them on the street. I was playing regular dance music in the street.

Yeah. But man, I'm telling you, Black Bennett, the way he played a drum, he made you think it was in a hall. Mm-hmm. See, he didn't beat like that. No, but he played a bass drum for all kinds of ways. Yeah. Black Bennett was a terrible bass drum man. And, I mean, it's like you said, that same piece they played for dancers. They played on the street. Yeah. Yeah. High society. They played on the street. They played on the dance. Yeah. They played on the street. They played on the dance. Yeah.

That's, that's very interesting because, uh, I never, I never did know when the blues came in on the street. I just thought it was always there. Well, they, they, they played on the, they play them now.
